findings.claim: Library of Congress Classification places Geomorphology (range GB400–GB649) within Class G (Geography. Anthropology. Recreation), specifically under Physical geography — not under class Q (Science/Geology).
findings.quote: Geography. Anthropology. Recreation--Physical geography--Geomorphology. Landforms. Terrain

findings.claim: Universal Decimal Classification places Geomorphology at 551.4 under class 55 (Earth Sciences. Geological sciences), with a see-also reference to 911.2 Physical geography rather than filing it there.
findings.quote: 551.4 Geomorphology. Study of the Earth's physical forms Including: Continents, islands. Landforms. Morphostructures. Mountains, valleys

findings.claim: ANZSRC 2020 Fields of Research (the Australian/NZ implementation of OECD FORD) assigns Geomorphology code 370901 ("Geomorphology and earth surface processes") under 3709 (Physical geography and environmental geoscience) within division 37 (EARTH SCIENCES).

OECD FORD (Frascati Manual 2015) lists Geomorphology implicitly under field 1.5 'Earth and related Environmental sciences' — a Natural Sciences category, distinct from 5.7 'Social and economic geography' where physical geography is sometimes placed.

Encyclopaedia Britannica treats Geomorphology as a branch of geology ('for full treatment, see geology: Geomorphology') and describes it as 'closely allied' with geophysics, volcanology, and sedimentology — not primarily with human geography.
findings.quote: geomorphology, scientific discipline concerned with the description and classification of the Earth's topographic features. A brief treatment of geomorphology follows. For full treatment, see geology: Geomorphology.

findings.claim: The International Association of Geomorphologists (IAG) frames geomorphology as explicitly interdisciplinary, while listing collaborative partnerships with both geoscience bodies (AGU, EGU, GSA) and the International Geographical Union — indicating it bridges earth sciences and geography without filing under either alone.
findings.quote: Geomorphology is the Interdisciplinary and Systematic Study of Landforms, their Landscapes and the Earth Surface Processes that create and change them

findings.claim: The European Geosciences Union (EGU) hosts Geomorphology as a full peer division (GM) alongside other earth-science divisions (Hydrology HS, Ocean Sciences OS, Seismology SM, Tectonics TS), institutionally positioning it within the geosciences rather than geography.
findings.quote: Geomorphology is the scientific study of land-surface features and the dynamic processes that shape them.

notes:
OVERALL PICTURE: The scheme-level split is stark and consistent: LCC (GB400–649) files geomorphology under Class G (Geography. Anthropology. Recreation), while UDC (551.4), OECD FORD/ANZSRC 2020 (370901 → 37 EARTH SCIENCES), and Britannica (cross-references to geology) all file it in Earth Sciences. The EGU institutional home (geosciences umbrella) also supports earth sciences. The IAG's own self-description as 'interdisciplinary' plus its dual-umbrella collaboration list (IGU for geography + AGU/EGU/GSA for geosciences) makes it a genuine interface source rather than a vote either way.

CLUSTER CONSISTENCY: Across both LCC and UDC, geomorphology, hydrology, and oceanography are treated identically — all three land in the same parent class. In LCC all three are in class G (Physical geography); in UDC all three are in class 55 (Earth Sciences). This means any consistent-cluster ruling will need to resolve the schema conflict at the level of the cluster, not at individual disciplines. Geomorphology is NOT uniquely geography-leaning compared to hydrology or oceanography in LCC.

GEOGRAPHY VS EARTH-SCIENCES SPLIT: The LCC class G placement is primarily a library organizational convention (physical geography as a sub-discipline of geography), whereas the scientific classification bodies (FORD/ANZSRC, EGU, Britannica→geology) treat it as earth sciences. Physical geography is the explicit bridge concept: in LCC it is a subdivision of class G; in UDC, physical geography (911.2) appears only as a cross-reference from 551.4, not as its classification home. ANZSRC names the parent class '3709 Physical geography and environmental geoscience' but places the whole group within 37 EARTH SCIENCES, not in a geography division. This suggests that 'physical geography' as a label bridges both but that the weight of scientific classification authority falls on earth sciences. A single part_of → field:earth-sciences at proposed/confidence 0.8 is defensible; section-13 dual membership (also part_of geography, if that node existed) would also be justified by the IAG interface finding and LCC evidence."
